# F4 · Captain and vice-captain calls

*Extracted verbatim from the PRD, which remains the single source of truth for every criterion below. Edit the PRD, then regenerate — never edit this file.*

Identifiers in this file: `F4-AC-01` – `F4-UP-02`.
Load alongside this file: `ENGINE.criteria.md`.

#### F4 · Captain and vice-captain calls

| Section | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Priority | **Must.** A named weekly decision in 2.1 that always renders, even as a keep reading. |
| Serves | The first core job in Section 2.3 — the captaincy decision. |
| Happy path | The Captain tab carries two calls, always. The armband and the vice armband are separate assignments that cannot be held by the same player, so each gets its own call. Each uses the same head-to-head layout, evaluation table and gestures as a transfer call. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **F4-AC-01** | Advice is given on both the captain and the vice-captain every week, even when the advice is to keep the current holder. |
| **F4-AC-02** | Where the advice is to keep, it renders as a reading rather than a decidable call: the decision panel shows a non-interactive "no change / nothing to do" label. |
| **F4-AC-03** | A keep reading is excluded from the editorial and from every tally, and the group meta reflects it — for example "1 pick · 1 held". |
| **F4-AC-04** | The evaluation rows are the master list, not a captaincy-specific set. |
| **F4-AC-05** | What is captaincy-specific is the reasoning block and the vice call's premise: eligibility, rotation risk, and the fact that the vice armband only pays if the captain does not play. |
| **F4-AC-06** | Captaincy calls have no candidate picker; the pair is fixed by the squad. |
| **F4-AC-07** | A captaincy pick is forced when, and only when, the current captain is ruled out (availability rating 0). |
| **F4-AC-08** | However high its conviction, a captaincy pick is never forced while the incumbent can play — an armband is always a choice. |
| **F4-AC-09** | A captaincy call costs nothing: no money moves and no transfer is used, so its cost reads £0.00. |
| **F4-AC-10** | The vice call resolves to a keep reading in almost every week, because a vice armband only pays when the captain does not play and that probability is small (the arithmetic is in the engine section). Where it does resolve to a change, it is a change like any other. |
| **F4-AC-11** | **The same calculation breakdown as F3-AC-30 and F3-AC-31 is available**, including which category's k value was used — captain/vice, not transfer — and Availability's source for each player. |
| **F4-AC-12** | Where the ceiling tie-break (3.2) chose the challenger, the reasoning says so and the calculation breakdown shows it, so a pick that is not the highest-xPts option is never unexplained. |
| **Unhappy Paths** |  |
| **F4-UP-01** | **The recommended captain has no fixture, or two.** Acceptance: handled by the same blank/double grammar as F1 — the *games this gameweek* row appears at the top of the evaluation table, the fixture row's winner follows who plays rather than who has the easier fixture, and projections sum or zero accordingly. |
| **F4-UP-02** | **The captain change is rejected.** Acceptance: the vice call becomes a keep reading rather than disappearing, so the manager is never left with an inconsistent armband pair. |
